## Natural history notes

A native perennial bunchgrass with tough, narrow, wiry leaves that form dense clumps and produce tall flowering stalks bearing three-awned seeds. Wire Grass is a characteristic groundcover of Florida’s pine flatwoods, sandhills, and other open, well-drained pine communities. It is strongly associated with frequent fire: the grass readily carries low-intensity ground fires, while growing-season burns can stimulate flowering and seed production. Because of this relationship, it plays an important role in maintaining the open structure and biodiversity of Florida’s fire-dependent longleaf pine ecosystems.
